source_span: You potentially have a supply shock hurting growth at the same time as the Fed is pushed toward tightening. Not a great backdrop for multiples... If the administration can get crude, gas and product prices lower, yields can stabilize and risk has a path to recover... provided NFP/CPI cooperate. If energy keeps rising, the Fed reaction function gets dragged with it and sustained upside becomes much harder.
source_chain: Iran strikes push crude/gas/distillates higher, therefore higher commodity inflation pulls the front end of the curve up as the market prices a real Fed response, therefore a supply shock hitting growth at the same time the Fed is pushed toward tightening is a poor backdrop for multiples; invalidation: if crude/gas/product prices fall, yields stabilize and risk has a path to recover provided NFP/CPI cooperate, but if energy keeps rising the Fed gets dragged with it and sustained upside gets harder.
pulse_chain: Iran strikes push Brent/gas higher, therefore that drags yields up (short and long end) because traders price a real chance the Fed responds, therefore Goldman's desk reads a supply shock hitting growth at the same moment policy is pushed toward tightening as a poor backdrop for what investors will pay for earnings, with sustained upside getting harder if energy keeps climbing (countered by JPM's activity-not-inflation-expectations read and TS Lombard's Taylor-rule read, both landing on less tightening); invalidation: if crude, gas and refined fuel prices come lower, yields can stabilize and risk assets can recover, provided payrolls and inflation cooperate.
why: The pulse reproduces Goldman's supply-shock-meets-tightening mechanism and its exact invalidation condition (energy down → yields stabilize → risk recovers, conditional on payrolls/inflation) with correct attribution, and layers in JPM's and TS Lombard's counter-arguments (verified against 15089 and 15098) without reversing either bank's claim or swapping the invalidation.
